newsitem.title: UK: GNI sees 1996/97 coffee crop at 99.4 mln bags.
newsitem.headline: GNI sees 1996/97 coffee crop at 99.4 mln bags.

text.p: Commodity brokers GNI estimated 1996/97 world coffee output at 99.4 million bags, up from 84.1 million in the previous season, but said supplies were likely to remain tight in coming months.
GNI saw consumption at a record 100.6 million bags for 1996/97, up slightly from 100.2 million in 1995/96.

This would result in a deficit of around 1.2 million bags for the season, compared with 16 million in 1995/96, despite a dramatic recovery in the Brazilian crop to a projected 27 million bags from 12.5 million.

"While consumer stocks should start their seasonal build in the near future, it is unlikely they will rise to the degree that many roasters are anticipating," GNI said in their December Commodity Perspective released on Monday.

Generally low consumer stocks should lift New York arabica futures to $1.30 and possibly even to $1.60 in coming months from around $1.07 now. But origin selling was likely to dampen the possibility of a further rally.
Estimates of the Brazilian crop in 1997/98 would also determine market sentiment although it was difficult to draw conclusions just yet from initially poor flowerings.
"Any "reliable' forecast calling for a sub-28.5 million bag crop should be viewed positively," GNI said.
A crop of around 26 million bags would result in a supply deficit of around 2.5 million bags which "gives enough room for the market to remain tight".
GNI said its 1996/97 estimate for Brazil of 27 million bags had some scope for downward revisions later in the year.

Higher crop projections by European traders implying a harvest of close to 28 million bags ignored the early picking of the crop which had the effect of bolstering the arrivals data and reducing yield, it said.

Brazil would be unable to ship its full ACPC (Association of Coffee Producing Countries) quota of 15 million bags if the government stuck to its current ceiling of 200,000 bags of stocks sales per month in the second half of the year.
"The action of the Brazilian government will clearly be critical in determining the level of international prices in the coming months," it said.
GNI forecast Indonesia's crop at eight million bags in 1996/97 from six million, Vietnam 500,000 bags higher at 4.5 million while Colombia was seen declining to 11.6 million bags from 12.9 million.
Small reductions were likely in several Central American countries after recent heavy rains but Mexico could harvest a crop slightly above five million bags.
